secondaryKeywords: incident management platform, incident response tooling, on-call rotation software, incident postmortem tool
jobToBeDone: coordinate the response when a critical service goes down, from the moment the alert fires to the moment the postmortem closes, without the team improvising in a chat channel
adjacentTools: Slack, Microsoft Teams, PagerDuty, Opsgenie, Jira, Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, Statuspage
productDescription: Guardia is an incident management platform for engineering teams of 15 to 300 people. It opens a dedicated channel the moment an alert arrives, assigns the response roles, records the timeline automatically and drafts the postmortem from what it already captured. It is used mostly by companies that have outgrown handling incidents by hand but do not want to stand up an enterprise-grade process.

features.name: Automatic incident channel
features.description: Creates the Slack or Teams channel when the alert arrives, pulls in whoever is on call and posts the alert context as the first message.

features.name: Response role assignment
features.description: Assigns incident commander, communications lead and operations lead, and keeps who holds each role visible for the whole response.

features.name: Automatic timeline
features.description: Records every status change, deploy and flagged decision in the channel with a timestamp, without anyone having to take notes.

features.name: Status page and customer updates
features.description: Publishes and updates the public status page from inside the incident channel, without switching tools.

features.name: Postmortem draft
features.description: Drafts the postmortem from the recorded timeline, with time-to-detect and time-to-resolve already calculated.

features.name: On-call rotation and escalation
features.description: Runs the on-call calendar, handovers and tiered escalation when the first responder does not acknowledge inside the set window.

integrations: Slack, Microsoft Teams, PagerDuty, Opsgenie, Jira, Linear, Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, GitHub Actions, Statuspage
pricingModel: per responder, from $24 per on-call responder per month, channel observers are free and there is no per-incident charge
implementationTime: one afternoon to the first real incident: the Slack and alerting connections take about 30 minutes and the on-call calendar imports from PagerDuty or Opsgenie
migrationNotes: Imports on-call calendars, escalation policies and services from PagerDuty and Opsgenie over API. Historical incidents can be loaded read-only to preserve metrics, but old timelines are not reconstructed.

testimonials.quote: The first fifteen minutes used to go on working out who was running it. Now that is already decided when you join the channel.
testimonials.author: Elena Saez

testimonials.quote: The postmortem writes itself from what already happened in the channel. We stopped arguing about the timeline.
testimonials.author: Ivan Torres

frictionStrippers: no credit card required and no production access needed for the trial
ctaRules: Name Guardia explicitly in the closing CTA and tie it to the reader's own on-call rotation. Never promise a specific reduction in resolution time, only report what named customers measured.
faqSeeds: How does Guardia actually work during an incident?
How long does it take to set up?
Can we migrate our on-call rotation from PagerDuty?
Does it replace PagerDuty or run alongside it?
What happens when an incident starts without an automated alert?
How are we billed if a lot of people are watching the channel?
writingPreferences: Address the reader as "you" and write to the person who is on call, not to their director. Never use "solution" as a noun. Do not use the phrase "engineering leaders".
